newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - Feb 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
GUN RAIDER IS GIVEN 150,000 FREE HOME

An armed robber who was shot and paralysed during raid on an Islington store has been given a 150,000 stg purpose-built house, just a few hundreds yards from the scene of his last crime. The house has been set up jointly by Islington Council, social services and a housing association, using money from Camden and Islington Health Authority.

Michael Price, the hard-driving mutual fund investor plans to increase his 1 percent shareholding in Pearson, if the media group has any more slip-ups like the recent accounting scandal at its Penguin books division.

Following the aftermath of China's leader Deng Xiaoping, Far East markets remained steady. The US currency staged a partial recovery. The yen slipped from its overnight 198.32 to 198.63 against the pound.
LLOYDS TSB TUNES INTO A TV REVOLUTION

TV banking goes live next Wednesday with Lloyds TSB running a trial with privately-owned broadband service provider Videonet. The service will provide Britain's only functioning dial-up 'video-on-demand' service.
